But JsonSchemaFactory.findMetaSchemaForSchema uses jsonMetaSchemas map and computeIfAbsent using fromId. The meta schema map contains the mock keyed by normalized URI. The defaultMetaSchemaURI will be normalized via normalizeMetaSchemaUri during builder? builder passes defaultMetaSchemaURI as given; but JsonSchemaFactory constructor validates that jsonMetaSchemas.get(normalizeMetaSchemaUri(defaultMetaSchemaURI)) != null. So we need to ensure key matches normalized version. So we should compute normalized version: JsonSchemaFactory.normalizeMetaSchemaUri("https://example.com/draft-07/schema") returns same (maybe). So we can put mock with key "https://example.com/draft-07/schema". Use builder().addMetaSchema(mock).build().

When adding meta schema, Builder.addMetaSchema normalizes the uri using normalizeMetaSchemaUri(jsonMetaSchema.getUri()). So we need to stub getUri() to return "https://example.com/draft-07/schema". Fine.

- testNormalizeMetaSchemaUriInvalid: malformed URI leads to JsonSchemaException.

- testIsYamlTrue: with .yaml/.yml extension.

- testIsYamlFalse: no extension or .json.

- testIdMatchesSourceUriTrue/False: need a JsonMetaSchema mock where readId returns string matching given uri.

- testGetSchemaStringValid: Use a simple JSON schema string e.g., "{}". It will call newJsonSchema which uses findMetaSchemaForSchema etc. It will need meta schema; we have mock meta schema; findMetaSchemaForSchema will look at "$schema" node; none, so defaultMetaSchemaURI used. Should succeed and return a JsonSchema instance (which is built inside factory). That will call JsonSchema.from which is part of library; may need actual implementation; likely returns real JsonSchema object that may depend on many other parts (keywords). Might be heavy.

That will use our custom fetcher to return InputStream.
